_meta.title: fix(stability): error rate 3,8% -> <1% ed eliminazione dei 25k dead click mensili
_meta.source: PostHog HogQL, project eu.posthog.com, live query, 30-day rolling window ending 2026-07-16
_meta.purpose: Baseline snapshot used to triage and fix issue #4304. NOT an accumulator — re-run the same HogQL queries for future audits rather than appending here.

This is the DIAGNOSTIC event emitted by the pre-existing self-heal path (services/resilientImport.ts / recoverFromStaleChunk) when it successfully detects and recovers from post-deploy cache skew, not an unrecovered crash.

Not root-caused — sample volume concentrated on one page, but stack unavailable (synthetic/no frames in the sampled events). Plausible stale-chunk-adjacent parse failure (partial/truncated JS response cached by SW or CDN) but not confirmed.
top10ErrorClusters.action: NOT IMPLEMENTED — needs a live reproduction (Playwright + network throttling/cache poisoning simulation) or a resolved stack sample before a safe fix can be written. Flagged for follow-up.

top10ErrorClusters.message: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
top10ErrorClusters.rootCause: Not root-caused. synthetic:true (window.onerror generic capture, no stack) across many unrelated pages — not page-specific, so likely a global recursive function. Coincides with elevated force_reload (1175/883) and chunk_retry (449/189) counts, suggesting a possible self-heal retry loop under specific timing (not confirmed).
top10ErrorClusters.action: NOT IMPLEMENTED — no stack trace available (synthetic error) and multi-page pattern rules out a single component; needs live reproduction to pin down safely. Flagged for follow-up rather than guessed at.

top10ErrorClusters.rootCause: services/analytics.ts's global unhandledrejection handler (~line 1070) fires on ANY Promise rejecting with a falsy/non-Error reason (e.g. `Promise.reject()`, `Promise.reject(null)`). No stack trace by design (the rejection reason itself carries none). 1:1 events:users pattern with no path/UA concentration — scattered, low-signal.
top10ErrorClusters.action: None applied. Root-causing which specific reject() call needs a first-party source audit for bare `Promise.reject()`/`.reject(falsy)` call sites — out of proportion to 30 events/30 users relative to the rest of the triage. Documented, not fixed.

top10ErrorClusters.message: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trackCalculation')
top10ErrorClusters.rootCause: Cross-chunk version skew left the Analytics lazy-proxy (services/analyticsProxy.ts) bound to undefined at the call site in a stale cached chunk.
top10ErrorClusters.action: FIXED — commit ab4d3890b9b: extended CALL_TIME_SKEW_PATTERNS in services/resilientImport.ts with V8 + Safari undefined-lazy-proxy TypeError shapes, anchored to the track*/init*/set* Analytics method naming convention. Mirrored in index.html's inline pre-module bootstrap. Routes through the existing recoverFromStaleChunk() self-heal instead of a dead top-level error screen.

additionalFixedThisSession.message: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'apply')
additionalFixedThisSession.rootCause: hooks/useUIState.ts and hooks/useSeoPageTracking.ts independently monkeypatch history.pushState/replaceState; under React StrictMode double-invocation or interleaved mount/unmount, the captured original*State reference could go stale by the time a navigation fired, throwing at .apply() and crashing to the top-level ErrorBoundary over a tracking call.
additionalFixedThisSession.action: FIXED — commit 6cac44e3ce0: guarded all 3 .apply() call sites (grep-verified exhaustive across services/components/hooks) with typeof === 'function' checks, no-op fallback. Regression tests added to tests/hooks/useUIState.test.ts and tests/useSeoPageTracking.test.ts.

topClusters.rootCause: The detector's `actionable` allowlist excluded native <select> (and <input>, <textarea>, <summary>), so every click on a fully-interactive native marital-status dropdown was unconditionally flagged dead regardless of whether the picker opened. Largest single cluster (~17% of all custom dead_click events).
topClusters.action: FIXED — commit a8af38ef3f3: widened actionable allowlist to select/input/textarea/summary.

topClusters.rootCause: components/calculator/ResultsView.tsx's BreakdownTable accordion row rendered a ChevronRight icon (lucide-react <svg>) inside a clickable div lacking role=button, so keyboard/AT-invisible clicks landing on the icon's <svg>/<path> resolved to a non-actionable element under the old detector allowlist. SVG className is an SVGAnimatedString, not a string, compounding the false-classification.
topClusters.action: FIXED as a side effect of commit 87d2e4ccae6 (role=button/tabIndex/onKeyDown added to the wrapping div) — clicks on the icon now correctly resolve via target.closest('[role="button"]').

topClusters.rootCause: Google Funding Choices (consent CMP) slider widget — third-party markup we do not own.
topClusters.action: FIXED — commit a8af38ef3f3: excluded via class-namespace guard (fc- prefix) in detectDeadClick().

topClusters.rootCause: input[type=range] slider — native, fully interactive, excluded from the old allowlist.
topClusters.action: FIXED — commit a8af38ef3f3 (allowlist widened to include input).

topClusters.note: Combines the 33/27 and 28/21 rows (same accordion row, two DOM sub-targets).
topClusters.rootCause: Same BreakdownTable accordion row as rank 2 — a clickable div without role=button/tabIndex/keyboard handler.
topClusters.action: FIXED as a side effect of commit 87d2e4ccae6.

topClusters.rootCause: Traced route to components/guide/BorderMunicipalitiesMap.tsx. Confirmed: no <svg>/cursor-pointer usage in the file at all; all 4 onClick handlers are on genuine semantic <button> elements already covered by the actionable allowlist; the municipality comparison cards (grid at line 704) are read-only display divs with NO onClick handler — selection happens via a <select> dropdown (compareMunicipality), not by clicking cards. The cards' className (bg-surface rounded-xl p-4 border ...) does not contain the literal substring 'card' or 'banner', so the detector's own looksClickable heuristic (cursor:pointer OR class*=card OR class*=banner) should not even match them.
topClusters.action: NOT FIXED — no missing-interactivity defect found in this component. Most likely explanation: mis-taps on decorative icons (Award/TrendingUp/TrendingDown/Building2) inside the read-only comparison cards, or a detector heuristic edge case not reproducible via static analysis. Needs live session-replay review to pin down further; low volume (~1% of custom dead-click total) does not justify a speculative code change.

topClusters.rootCause: Native <details>/<summary> disclosure widgets — already fully interactive/keyboard-accessible by browser default. Confirmed false positive on manual read (documented in commit 87d2e4ccae6's message: 'Remaining ~20 candidates ... backdrop/scrim dismiss-click, modal-content stopPropagation guards, third-party Google-Sign-In button container').
Google Translate's DOM-wrapping spans around already-instrumented first-party elements.

cssFallback.byPagePath: Scattered across 25+ job-detail/hub URLs, none dominating (top: /cerca-lavoro-ticino/infermieri/, 26/17). No single page or template concentrates the failures.

diagnosis.ruledOut: Single-browser-engine onload bug — the Chrome-Android/Mobile-Safari-iOS split (461 vs 388) is roughly proportional to the site's actual mobile traffic mix, not concentrated in one rendering engine.
diagnosis.weakened: Pure slow-network cause — 93% of events self-report navigator.connection.effectiveType='4g', but this API is a Chromium-only (not Safari/Firefox) SOFT HEURISTIC that defaults to '4g' absent contrary evidence, not a hard measurement, so it does not conclusively rule out network-related causes on the ~44% of events from Mobile Safari (which has no Network Information API support at all and is silently bucketed 'unknown' or defaults elsewhere).
diagnosis.openHypothesis: Background-tab throttling — mobile OSes deprioritize timers/fetches for backgrounded tabs, which could delay both the onload firing AND (less likely) the setTimeout fallback itself. NOT verifiable with existing telemetry (no visibility-state dimension existed before this session).

cssFallback.action: MITIGATED (diagnostic-only, no behavior change) — commit pending in this session: added `visibilityState: document.visibilityState` to the _cssFallbackInfo payload (build-plugins/htmlTemplate.ts's ASYNC_CSS_FALLBACK_SCRIPT, drained by services/analytics.ts's trackCssFallback). document.visibilityState (Page Visibility API) is universally supported, unlike Network Information API. Deliberately did NOT change the 3000ms timeout value — no evidence a different value would help, and changing it risks worsening FOUC for the majority (893/956, ~93%) of unaffected fast-connection sessions. Re-query cssFallbackByVisibilityState once this instrumentation has ~7-14 days of live data to confirm/rule out the background-tab-throttling hypothesis.
cssFallback.siblingPatternFixThisSession: Discovered AGENTS.md #6 violation: build-plugins/ogPagesPlugin.ts and build-plugins/staticPagesPlugin.ts had literal byte-for-byte duplicate copies of the ASYNC_CSS_FALLBACK_SCRIPT setTimeout text instead of importing the shared build-plugins/htmlTemplate.ts constant (the two copies had already drifted before this fix). Refactored both to import ASYNC_CSS_FALLBACK_SCRIPT; added a regression test (tests/build-plugins/asyncCssLandings.test.ts) locking the import in place. Verified the SPA's own build-plugins/asyncCssPlugin.ts does NOT emit this telemetry at all — all 956/30d events originate exclusively from static SEO page emitters.
